h: How to slide like a pro
p: Shuffleboard is all about touch. Rather than shoving the puck, try a smooth, steady push and let it glide down the table, following through in a straight line. The aim is to land in the high-scoring zones without sailing off the end. Once you've got a feel for the pace, start playing tactically: leave blockers, knock out your opponent's best puck, or nudge your own puck into a better spot. It's amazing how quickly things get competitive.

Groups should think about booking early, especially for Friday nights and the run-up to Christmas, when the arches are popular for office parties. Order food before the game hots up so nobody's juggling plates and pucks, and set teams that mix experienced players with newcomers to keep scores close. Age policies vary at venues like this, so check with the team first if anyone in your party is under 18.

The London Bridge area has some lovely surprises nearby. Southwark Cathedral, right next to Borough Market, is a beautiful medieval church and a peaceful contrast to the busy streets. Hay's Galleria and the riverside path give great views of Tower Bridge and HMS Belfast, and at weekends the Maltby Street food market sets up under the railway arches a short walk east of Bermondsey Street. If you're a fan of design, the Fashion and Textile Museum on Bermondsey Street has changing exhibitions, while the Shard's viewing gallery offers a dramatic view over the city. With so much on the doorstep, you could easily build a whole day around your evening game.
